title: Put the sample cuvette in the spectrophotometer: held only by its frosted sides, turned a quarter turn
instruction: Put the sample in the spectrophotometer.
context: Absorbance readings in a 1 cm cuvette are among the most common lab measurements, and instrument manuals are explicit: "Handle cuvettes on the frosted sides only. Place the cuvette into the chamber so that the "reading" (clear) sides face left and right" (Molecular Devices SpectraMax user guide). A cell put in the wrong way round sends the beam through its frosted sides, and a pad mark on a window scatters the light; either way the reading is wrong. The instruction only says to put the sample in: the cuvette has to be held by its frosted sides, turned a quarter turn, kept upright (it is open and three-quarters full) and lowered into a well 1.75 mm wider than it on each side. About 571,000 US jobs (clinical lab technologists and technicians, biological and chemical technicians, chemists; BLS OOH 2025) do this routinely, and it is a core step for lab robots.
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. A UV-Vis spectrophotometer (a 20 x 24 cm body, 7 cm tall, 4 kg, loose) stands at x 34, y -2; its cuvette chamber is open: a 16 mm square well 1.5 cm deep (its top 5 mm opening to 22 mm) at x 28, y -10, its floor 5.5 cm up, with bold orange arrows (8 mm wide, 7 cm long) either side showing the beam running right to left (along y). A standard 1 cm cuvette (12.5 mm square, 45 mm tall, 4.5 g with about 3 ml of pink sample, loose) stands in a shallow blue plastic cuvette tray (a 6 x 6 cm plate with one 32 mm square well 8 mm deep, 150 g, loose) at x 40, y -24. Two of the cuvette's sides are frosted white, the other two clear; in the rack the clear sides face front and back (along x).
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial if at any moment a gripper is closed on the cuvette with its pads on the clear windows (its closing axis within 45 deg of the windows' normal), the cuvette tips more than 25 deg (an open, three-quarters-full cell spills), falls faster than 0.6 m/s (dropped) or ends on the table. Otherwise: 1.0 for the cuvette seated on the well's floor (within 2 mm) with its clear sides within 10 deg of facing the beam, let go (both grippers 3 cm or more away) and still; 0.5 for it in the well, so turned, but not seated or still held; 0.25 for it lifted out of the tray and held; 0 otherwise, including seated with the beam through its frosted sides. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. On a real bench, the clear windows dusted with talc show any pad mark, and an overhead camera reads the cuvette's turn against the arrows and its tilt.
reset_notes: Wipe the cuvette's windows, re-dust them, and stand it back in the tray the same way round.
fidelity: The cuvette is one rigid box of the right size and mass; the sample is drawn only (no liquid), so spilling is judged by tilt past 25 deg. The chamber's centring spring is left out: the well is a fixed 16 mm square (1.75 mm play a side) with a 5 mm, 22 mm lead-in at its top. PhysX point contacts give a flat pad no grip against turning, so the cuvette's contacts get a 6 mm torsional-friction patch (without it the cuvette spun to its diagonal in the pads).
scores: Dream-1 flash: 0.0. Scripted demo 1.0, naive 0.0, unsafe 0.0 (Isaac Sim, re-checked 18 Nov 2026 at 320x176 after a scene revision). That Dream run had stretched 224x224 cameras; re-run pending. Details in README.
